title: RLM (Recursive Language Models) Architecture Integration
description:
Integrate MIT's RLM paradigm into MAIA/AIN for scalable context handling, long-horizon tasks, and corpus-as-environment capabilities.

## Why RLM fits MAIA
- Treats large context as external environment model can query/manipulate
- Recursive self-calls over relevant slices instead of swallowing everything
- Maps to existing orchestrator + tools + memory architecture

## Key Benefits
1. Near-infinite context without accuracy degradation
2. Codebase-level intelligence (recursive grep/read/patch)
3. Better long-horizon agent behavior (AIN deliberations)

## Implementation Targets
- Community Commons (manuals, docs, member knowledge)
- Session transcripts (long conversations without context rot)
- Codebase operations (recursive navigation vs one-shot RAG)

## Resources
- Paper: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.24601v1
- Library: https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm
- Blog: https://www.primeintellect.ai/blog/rlm

## Security Considerations
- REPL/sandbox must respect MAIA sovereignty constraints
- Local-first, no external cloud
- Tool guardrails for code execution
close_reason: Phase 1 complete: RCN routing logic (rcnRouter.ts), MAIA wrapper (rcnIntegration.ts), and maiaService.ts integration. Intent detection, corpus type routing, non-blocking fallback to FAST/CORE/DEEP paths.

- Latency impact of service boundary
- Docker containerization for sovereignty
- How this fits with existing lib/ai/ architecture
